name: Circuit product capability model
purpose: Connect product intent to capabilities, current surfaces, proof, gaps, overlaps, and deliberate boundaries.

vision.title: Encode the process
vision.statement: Turn a known way of working into a repeatable, invokable, adjustable flow.

vision.title: Fit the worker to the step
vision.statement: Give each step the right role, context, tools, connector, model, and effort.

vision.title: Require proof before progress
vision.statement: Do not advance or close until the declared evidence exists and parses.

vision.title: Carry the operational load
vision.statement: Carry routing, state, coordination, recovery, and continuity outside the chat.

vision.title: Improve from experience
vision.statement: Use evidence from real runs to improve the process that runs next time.

areas.title: Shape intent into a repeatable process
areas.summary: Move from an operator's intent to an authored process with a clear boundary and proof plan.

areas.title: Apply skilled work patterns
areas.summary: Offer proven processes for recurring kinds of product and engineering work.

areas.title: Equip and coordinate agents
areas.summary: Give each step the right working conditions and coordinate bounded forms of parallel and repeated work.

areas.title: Preserve confidence and continuity
areas.summary: Make work understandable before it starts and recoverable after pauses, failures, or session changes.

areas.title: Prove and explain outcomes
areas.summary: Check the work, judge it separately, and leave an honest record of what happened.

areas.title: Learn and improve from experience
areas.summary: Capture useful lessons, bring them back at the right time, and improve flows from real evidence.

areas.title: Configure and operate Circuit
areas.summary: Keep Circuit understandable, ready, configurable, and removable across supported environments.

capabilities.title: Route a request into the right flow
capabilities.summary: Turn an operator request into the most suitable authored process.

attention.note: The host can help choose, but the CLI still expects the caller to name a flow. The intake and route blocks are authored vocabulary no shipped flow executes yet; routing happens in the host model today.

capabilities.title: Frame the outcome, limits, and proof
capabilities.summary: Turn a rough request into a bounded brief with a declared way to prove success.

capabilities.title: Encode typed flows from blocks, routes, and checks
capabilities.summary: Describe a reusable process as authored topology with typed seams and evidence requirements.

attention.note: Typed-flow authoring is source-checkout work today. The public path to a custom flow is create and generate, mapped under the flow lifecycle.

capabilities.title: Create, customize, publish, and manage flows
capabilities.summary: Carry a custom process through a complete lifecycle, not just its first generation.

attention.note: A draft, review, edit, and publish loop exists; version, share, supersede, retire, and host publication do not yet form one lifecycle.

capabilities.title: Audit existing work
capabilities.summary: Inspect a bounded body of work and report evidence-backed findings without changing it.

capabilities.title: Fix broken behavior
capabilities.summary: Diagnose a fault, change the smallest useful surface, and verify the repair.

capabilities.title: Build a change
capabilities.summary: Frame, implement, verify, and review a deliberate product or engineering change.

capabilities.title: Explore a question or decision
capabilities.summary: Gather evidence, compare real options, and make a bounded recommendation.

capabilities.title: Prototype and compare disposable solutions
capabilities.summary: Build a cheap learning artifact and use it to choose what deserves a real implementation.

capabilities.title: Own a bounded outcome across several pieces of work
capabilities.summary: Keep pursuing a declared outcome through bounded attempts, evaluation, and recovery.

attention.note: Goal is frozen internal: its contract and gate semantics now ship inside the run envelope, and the flow remains for compatibility and explicit internal runs. The open question is Pursue's public shape.

capabilities.title: Craft explanatory artifacts for humans
capabilities.summary: Turn source material into a polished artifact made for human readers rather than code review.

attention.note: Explainer stays internal: its editorial stages generalize, its delivery plumbing does not yet.

capabilities.title: Run isolated, role-shaped steps with scoped context and tools
capabilities.summary: Give a worker only the role, context, skills, and tools needed for one bounded step.

capabilities.title: Allocate connector, model, and effort per step
capabilities.summary: Choose the worker and spend level from the step's role, with explicit overrides when needed.

attention.note: cross-tool-build is an internal proof flow. The public delivery is per-step selection inside run and preview.

capabilities.title: Sequence, route, nest, and continue work within authored bounds
capabilities.summary: Execute an authored graph whose next steps are constrained by declared routes and child-flow seams.

capabilities.title: Fan out and compare alternatives
capabilities.summary: Run bounded alternatives independently, gather comparable evidence, and join them for a decision.

attention.note: The run-level tournament flag is the trigger; public flows default it off.

capabilities.title: Iterate until declared evidence passes
capabilities.summary: Repeat a bounded body while its authored condition says the proof is not yet sufficient.

attention.note: Every delivering flow is internal; a public converge surface is a named launch work item, not shipped. Loops carry fail-closed spend caps.

capabilities.title: Queue and batch broad work
capabilities.summary: Turn broad work into ordered items and process a bounded set with explicit outcomes.

attention.note: The mechanics exist as internal building blocks; the public product intent is not settled. The queue block itself is wired into no flow yet.

capabilities.title: Route runtime signals to the operator's skills
capabilities.summary: Fire a declared hook when a runtime signal matches and inject the operator's skill into the next relevant worker step.

capabilities.title: Scale rigor and spend to the stakes
capabilities.summary: Set how much process and model power a run deserves, or let the run recommend a level within declared limits.

capabilities.title: Adapt a running flow within bounds
capabilities.summary: Let a confirmed runtime discovery adjust later steps' skills, or let a step pull one typed context slice, without changing the authored topology.

attention.note: Budget-bounded runtime channels; routes, contracts, and workers never change mid-run.

capabilities.title: Preview execution before spending
capabilities.summary: Show the planned worker, connector, model, and effort choices without starting a run.

attention.note: The selection story is visible, but dependable time and cost estimates are not.

capabilities.title: Pause only for useful operator decisions
capabilities.summary: Ask a bounded question at a declared checkpoint and preserve the answer as evidence.

capabilities.title: Run unattended within authored bounds
capabilities.summary: Auto-resolve supported checkpoints in a bounded continuation loop that can never close complete by exhaustion.

capabilities.title: Resume work parked at a checkpoint
capabilities.summary: Continue the same durable run from a declared checkpoint, including after a host restart.

attention.note: A run interrupted before any checkpoint cannot be resumed; the only path is a fresh run that salvages finished branches. Mid-run crash durability is a separate open workstream.

capabilities.title: Carry work across sessions
capabilities.summary: Persist the state, evidence, and next action another session needs to continue safely.

attention.note: Continuity is host-asymmetric: Claude captures ambiently with zero setup; Codex is restore-only and needs a one-time hooks install.

capabilities.title: Capture session state automatically
capabilities.summary: Harvest a continuity record from the live session with no operator action, as a safety net under deliberate handoffs.

attention.note: Claude captures with zero setup; Codex does not capture by design, and its restore path needs a one-time hooks install.

capabilities.title: Recover and clean up safely
capabilities.summary: Choose a bounded recovery path and reclaim resources without hiding unfinished work.

attention.note: The risk-rollback-check block is authored vocabulary no shipped flow executes yet. Crash salvage into a fresh run rides the run command, not resume.

capabilities.title: Watch, answer, and safely cancel a live run
capabilities.summary: Hold one durable handle on a running piece of work to watch it, answer it, detach from it, and cancel it without corrupting state.

attention.note: Held for after v1; needs a local process that owns the run lifecycle.

capabilities.title: Run deterministic checks
capabilities.summary: Execute declared proof commands and capture their result as run evidence.

capabilities.title: Judge results independently
capabilities.summary: Separate doing the work from deciding whether the result satisfies its brief.

capabilities.title: Block false claims of done
capabilities.summary: Check worker claims against ground truth and refuse a clean close while any overclaim or tampered proof stands.

capabilities.title: Close honestly with evidence, risks, and follow-ups
capabilities.summary: End with an outcome the available evidence supports, explained in operator-readable close-out artifacts, and preserve what remains unresolved.

capabilities.title: Inspect recorded and active runs
capabilities.summary: Find past and current work, inspect its trace and evidence, and understand what needs attention.

attention.note: Recorded history is strong, and an attached run can be followed live; reconnectable watching, cancellation, and safe mid-run steering are not shipped.

capabilities.title: Follow a run while it happens
capabilities.summary: Stream structured progress events from an attached run so the operator or host can watch work as it happens.

attention.note: Attached-only today: detach, reconnect, and cancellation wait on the live-run control proposal.

capabilities.title: Capture operator lessons with evidence provenance
capabilities.summary: Record a durable lesson and preserve where it came from so it can be judged later.

capabilities.title: Reuse relevant evidence from earlier runs
capabilities.summary: Bring prior facts and lessons into later work without making the operator reconstruct them from chat.

capabilities.title: Measure whether a lesson helped
capabilities.summary: Judge each remembered lesson against later run outcomes and stop surfacing the ones that measurably hurt.

capabilities.title: Measure, promote, and improve flows
capabilities.summary: Use evidence from completed work to create or revise a reusable process with a measurable reason.

attention.note: This is the missing link between durable run evidence and a compounding product loop.

capabilities.title: Configure routing, connectors, models, power, and skills
capabilities.summary: Set the defaults and policies that determine how flows are equipped and run, including registering custom connectors as workers.

capabilities.title: Check readiness, version, and runtime provenance
capabilities.summary: Explain whether Circuit can run here, which build is active, and what needs to be fixed.

capabilities.title: Maintain or remove the installation and leftover resources
capabilities.summary: Keep installed host bridges and local run resources understandable and removable.

attention.note: Installation is currently host-plugin-led, while maintenance utilities remain CLI-led. Install and first-run onboarding have no capability row of their own yet.

capabilities.title: Operate the same flows from multiple agent hosts
capabilities.summary: Drive one encoded process from Claude Code or Codex through mirrored host surfaces, with worker selection aware of the host.

attention.note: Continuity capture is Claude-only today, and exposure values cannot yet say which host reaches what.

capabilities.title: Orient and discover without reading docs
capabilities.summary: Give a bare invocation, a piped agent, or a lost operator a guided path to the right next command.

attention.note: Bare invocation and help sit outside the 15-command vocabulary, so the surface audit cannot see them.

boundaries.title: No fully dynamic runtime-composed workflows
boundaries.reason: Circuit prefers authored topology with typed seams over an open-ended runtime classifier.

boundaries.title: No git-push interception
boundaries.reason: Circuit routes work through deliberately invoked flows rather than a hook that captures every push.

boundaries.title: No keep-best optimization loop without an ungameable judge
boundaries.reason: Exhaust-and-keep-best would weaken the evidence and honesty model without a trustworthy oracle.

boundaries.title: No mid-task model switching by runtime guess
boundaries.reason: Worker allocation is authored per step rather than delegated to an opaque runtime classifier.

boundaries.title: Memory guides, never governs
boundaries.reason: Recalled lessons are cited hints; they never change routes, checkpoints, or proofs, and Circuit claims no self-improvement until measured effect earns it.

boundaries.title: No universal percentage and no invented ETA
boundaries.reason: Progress reports known structure only; an estimate appears only when flow-specific evidence supports it.

boundaries.title: No generic pause button and no free-form mid-worker steering
boundaries.reason: Mid-run influence arrives only through declared checkpoints and bounded channels, not an open steering wheel.

boundaries.title: Hosts never become the orchestrator
boundaries.reason: Host-native execution stays an adapter under Circuit's authority so every client shares one capability model.

review_questions.question: Should Run become the one product front door that chooses a flow, or should explicit flow choice remain part of the contract?
What is the smallest complete custom-flow lifecycle worth making public?
With Goal frozen into the run envelope, what public shape, if any, should Pursue and its queue-and-batch machinery take?
Which internal coordination mechanics deserve a public product surface, and which should remain implementation proof?
Does active-run control belong in Circuit v2, or should Circuit remain primarily a durable record plus resume engine?
What evidence must exist before the learning loop is allowed to change a flow?
Which CLI-only utilities are real product surfaces, and which are maintenance details that should stay out of the primary map?
Should Circuit compute dependable per-run time and cost estimates, or does cost candor stay static documentation?
Which capabilities must reach both hosts at parity, and where is asymmetry acceptable?
